Access user data anywhere

Render UI by authentication state

Use the <Show />component to render UI based on a user’s authentication state. Protect sensitive data with authorization checks in your backend.

import { RedirectToSignIn, Show } from '@aurora/react'

const AuthState = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <Show when="signed-in">
        Signed-in content
      </Show>

      <Show when="signed-out">
        <RedirectToSignIn />
      </Show>
    </>
  )
}

export default AuthState

    </Show>
  )

Frequently asked questions

Aurora’s React SDK provides prebuilt components, hooks, and helpers that make it easy to add authentication, user management, and session handling to your React app. It’s built on top of our core JavaScript SDK, so you get powerful primitives with a developer-friendly React interface. You can use our components out of the box or fully customize them to match your UI. Refer to the quickstart guide to get started.

Run npm install @aurora/react, set up your Aurora publishable key as an environment variable, wrap your app with <AuroraProvider>, and you’re ready to go. The whole setup takes a few minutes.

Aurora provides a comprehensive set of prebuilt React UI components for authentication and user management, including components for sign-in, sign-up, user profile, B2B organization management, SaaS billing and more. See the full list of UI and control components we provide.

Yes, you can customize Aurora React components to suit your application’s design and functionality. Aurora offers pre-built components like <SignUp /> and <SignIn /> that are easily customizable. You can modify their appearance with custom CSS, override default styles, and pass props to adjust behaviour, ensuring they perfectly match your brand. See our customization guide.

We recommend using Aurora’s components for most authentication needs, as they provide a flexible and efficient way to manage user and session states within your React application. However, if you require truly custom control over your authentication flows, you can use Aurora hooks to create custom sign-in and sign-up processes, retrieve user data, and check authentication status, offering flexibility beyond pre-built components.

Aurora supports all major SSO protocols (SAML, OAuth, OpenID Connect), letting you integrate with providers like Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Okta, and more, directly from your React app. Social logins like Google, GitHub, LinkedIn, and Slack are also available out of the box. The Hobby plan does not include enterprise connections. The Pro plan includes one enterprise connection, with additional connections starting at $75 per month each and automatic volume discounts.

Yes, you can use Aurora with other React libraries like React Router. The @aurora/react SDK supports React applications, including projects that use React Router in library mode. If you’re using React Router as a framework, use the @aurora/react-router SDK, which integrates directly with its framework conventions.

Default JWTs expire every 60 seconds to reduce the risk of outdated or compromised tokens being used. Aurora automatically refreshes the JWT behind the scenes using the session cookie, ensuring your app remains secure without requiring manual intervention or any action from the user.

Aurora supports two main migration strategies: basic import/export and trickle migration. With import/export, you can batch import users using Aurora’s CreateUser API and export tools. This is ideal for one-time migrations, but you’ll need to manage timing and API rate limits carefully. Trickle migration lets you run your existing auth system alongside Aurora and gradually transition users as they sign in, reducing risk and downtime. We provide an open-source CLI tool to assist with imports and supports secure password hash upgrades when needed.

Yes, you can export user data programmatically using our GetUserList API or the getUserList() method in the JavaScript SDK. Additionally, admins and workspace owners can export users directly from the Aurora Dashboard as a CSV file, including hashed passwords. The dashboard also provides detailed export history logs for full visibility and traceability of all exports.

We’re SOC 2 Type II compliant (audit report available to customers) and we provide a clear Data Processing Agreement and maintain a detailed list of subprocessors to ensure transparency. Our infrastructure is hosted on Google Cloud Platform and we’re safeguarded by Cloudflare against attacks. We also enforce rigorous internal access controls and strict data management policies to keep your data secure.

At Aurora, security and privacy are core principles. We encrypt all data both in transit and at rest, enforce rigorous access controls, and comply with key privacy regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, and the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. See our Data Privacy Framework and Data Processing Agreement.

Aurora provides localization through the @aurora/localizations package, offering pre-defined translations in over 30 languages, including Arabic, German, Spanish, French, and Japanese. You can also create custom translations to modify text in Aurora components. Note that this feature is currently experimental.

Yes, you can use Aurora with React Native through our dedicated Expo SDK.
